vm_tools: Put ARCVM processes in a proper cpu cgroup This CL bind-mounts host's |session_manager_container| cpu cgroup into Concierge. The cgroup is for Chrome to throttle Android processes (both ARC++ and ARCVM) based on its active window state etc. The CL also modifies Concierge's ARCVM code so that it adds ARCVM's crosvm process to |session_manager_container| group right after fork() but before execve(). With that, the first crosvm process and all its children will belong to the right cpu cgroup instead of the default one, /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/vms. Alternatives considered: Move ARCVM's crosvm process(es) somewhere outside Concierge. => This doesn't work well because the PID of crosvm Concierge knows is for Concierge's own PID namespace. The PID is useless outside Concierge, and the outside process in the init PID namespace has to scan through /proc/<pid> entries to find the crosvm process. Also, crosvm spawns threads and child processes after it's executed. Moving all of them without introducing races is a messy job. OTOH, if we change the crosvm's cpu cgroup before execve() (which is what this CL does), we don't have the race issue. BUG=b:135608119 TEST=Start arcvm, observe both /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/vms/tasks and /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/session_manager_containers/tasks, verify all ARCVM crosvm processes are in the latter group. Change-Id: Idf5f78f278e6018c70baddfea97ee1c744a60059 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1742996 Tested-by: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Philippe Liard <pliard@google.com>

firmware_ECBootTime: add a delay before pressing the power button As we changes the shutdown behavior for the mt8183 (ref cl:1660070), the system will stay in S5 for 10s before entering G3. So, when we do firmware_ECBootTime test, it will fail because the system is in S5 and the test script can't capture the string 'power state 1 = S5". To adopt the EC change, this patch adds a delay to force the mt8183 enters G3 before pressing power button. BUG=b:137605499 TEST=Pass the firmware_ECBootTime Change-Id: I01f77a3c04a880c42fc3f39fed24a4677c063789 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1743610 Tested-by: Zhuohao Lee <zhuohao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Zhuohao Lee <zhuohao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com>

UPSTREAM: drm/i915/skl: Fix has_ipc on skl and document WaDisableIPC. According to Spec for SKL+: "Isochronous Priority Control. If enabled, Display sends demoted requests once the transition watermark is reached. If transition watermark is not enabled, Display sends demoted requests when the display buffer is full." The commit 'e57f1c02155f ("drm/i915/gen9+: Add has_ipc flag in device info structure")' introduced that as gen9+ but missing many SKL Skus. I believe the reason for that is Spec also mentions workarounds for SKL-ALL: "IPC (Isoch Priority Control) may cause underflows WA: Do not enable IPC in register ARB_CTL2" It seems lame to add the feature and forever disable it, but it will avoid a mistake of enabling it when we are reorganizing the feature definitions on i915_pci.c later. It will also allow us to probably extend that workaround for other platforms. lib: cros_config: Add new cros_config_probe for mosys callback Almost all platforms using cros_config have same probing logic, which can be moved into a single place. The new cros_config may simplify the boilerplate for probe function in most platforms with one single call: return cros_config_probe(intf, platform_names); It is also true that on most Unified Build platforms, the 'platform name' in cros_config model.yaml file is exactly the same as intf->name, so for mosys interfaces that are not shared by multiple overlays (Unified Build platform name is usually the overlay name), we even don't need to pass the platform names: return cros_config_probe(intf, NULL); This eliminates the need of splitting probing process into (1) match SMBIOS or firmware name in probe stage, and (2) really call cros_config_read_sku_info later or in post.
